metadata.title: PyTorch AI Governance Component Definition
metadata.remarks: Component definition derived from PyTorch Governance Benchmark

components.title: PyTorch
components.description: AI/ML component for PyTorch with governance controls

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure baseline quality metrics are logged for every PyTorch training run

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Use PyTorch evaluation workflows to measure task quality on a held-out validation set for every model version before promotion.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Accuracy, F1-score, BLEU, ROUGE, exact match, perplexity

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Run the approved validation benchmark after training and compare model metrics to the approved baseline or previous champion model.

props.name: HF_Metric
props.value: Accuracy, F1-score, BLEU, ROUGE, Exact Match, Perplexity

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure candidate model quality metrics deviate by no more than 10% from the approved Hugging Face model-card baseline or internal champion baseline.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch is the training framework, so quality benchmarking is one of the most direct and relevant controls.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure train and validation curves are monitored for divergence

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Monitor training and validation loss and accuracy across epochs so exploding loss, stalled learning, or severe overfitting is detected early.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Train-validation loss gap, gradient norm, variance across epochs

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compute training and validation metrics per epoch and track sustained divergence, oscillation, or numerical instability over the full training run.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure sustained train-validation divergence remains below threshold and gradient instability does not exceed approved limits.

props.name: Threshold_Value
props.value: <10% sustained divergence; project-approved gradient norm range

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch directly exposes the training loop and autograd behavior, making this a core framework-level risk control.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure train, validation, and test split integrity is validated before training

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Validate dataset partitions for overlap, duplication, or contamination before using PyTorch DataLoader pipelines for model development.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Duplicate rate, train-test overlap rate, contamination rate

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compute overlap statistics across dataset splits and reject or flag model runs whose input data fails integrity checks.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure train-test overlap and contamination rates remain below threshold before model training is approved.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: This is highly relevant to PyTorch training pipelines, though it is not typically described in model cards.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure subgroup representation metrics are measured before model training

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Evaluate training and validation data for underrepresented groups or categories before training begins.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Coverage ratio, class imbalance ratio, subgroup sample proportion

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compute subgroup proportions and compare them to the approved representativeness target or expected production mix.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure subgroup coverage remains within approved representativeness thresholds before model training is approved.

props.name: Threshold_Value
props.value: No subgroup below 80% of expected coverage

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch itself does not ensure representativeness, but the training workflow depends on these dataset properties.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure gradient correctness is validated for custom operations and losses

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Use numerical or analytical gradient checks for custom autograd functions, losses, or layers before including them in production training pipelines.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Gradient-check pass rate, relative gradient error

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Run gradcheck or equivalent numerical validation on custom autograd components and compare computed gradients to reference gradients.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure all custom differentiable components pass gradient validation and remain within approved numerical tolerances.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorchâ€™s autograd system is a defining capability, so custom gradient correctness is a framework-specific risk area.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure representative training runs are profiled before scale-out

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Use PyTorch profiling tools to identify bottlenecks in operators, input pipelines, memory use, and device utilization before large-scale training.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Step time, GPU utilization, memory usage, data-loader stall time

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Profile representative training runs and compute average step time, utilization, memory consumption, and pipeline idle or wait time.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure representative training runs meet approved step-time and utilization targets before scale-out.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch provides profiler support, making this a direct performance-governance control.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure NaN, Inf, and exploding-gradient conditions are detected during training and evaluation

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Monitor tensors, losses, and gradients for NaN, Inf, or numerical blow-up conditions so unstable models are identified before deployment.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: NaN occurrence rate, Inf occurrence rate, gradient explosion rate

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Count numerical anomaly events across steps or batches and divide by total monitored steps or batches.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure numerical anomaly rates remain below the approved tolerance during training and validation.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: This risk is especially important in custom PyTorch training loops and distributed or mixed-precision setups.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure mixed-precision models retain approved task quality relative to FP32 baselines

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Benchmark AMP or other reduced-precision training or inference configurations against the FP32 reference before promotion.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Accuracy retention, perplexity delta, exact-match delta

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Retention = reduced-precision metric / FP32 baseline metric; compute quality deltas over the approved benchmark set.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure mixed-precision quality retention remains above threshold for approved training and inference modes.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch natively supports mixed precision, so precision-specific regression checks are highly relevant.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure distributed training runs converge consistently across ranks and nodes

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Validate that DistributedDataParallel or other supported distributed workflows converge consistently and do not silently diverge across workers.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Cross-rank loss variance, convergence deviation, distributed run pass rate

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compare loss curves and final model metrics across repeated distributed runs or across ranks to quantify instability or inconsistent convergence.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure distributed training convergence remains within the approved deviation threshold relative to the single-node or reference baseline.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch officially supports distributed training, so distributed correctness is a legitimate framework-specific control area.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure distributed communication overhead is profiled for representative training jobs

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Profile distributed communication primitives and all-reduce overhead so scale-out inefficiencies are visible before production training.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Communication overhead ratio, all-reduce time, scaling efficiency

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Communication overhead ratio = communication time / total step time; scaling efficiency compared against baseline throughput at smaller scale.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure distributed communication overhead remains within approved scaling targets for the planned cluster size.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: This is directly tied to torch.distributed and DDP support in PyTorch.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure torch.compile outputs preserve approved task quality

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Benchmark compiled models against eager-mode baselines to detect regressions introduced by graph capture, graph breaks, or backend compilation differences.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Accuracy retention, graph-break rate, output parity

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compare task metrics and output parity between eager-mode and compiled runs over the approved benchmark set; record graph breaks observed during compilation.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure compiled-model task quality remains within threshold of the approved eager baseline and graph-break behavior is reviewed.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: Official torch.compile guidance notes graph breaks as lost optimization opportunities, so quality and parity checks are appropriate after compilation.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure torch.compile speedup claims are validated on representative workloads

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Measure compiled-model performance on representative inputs so deployment decisions are based on real speedup rather than assumed improvements.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Latency improvement, throughput improvement, compile overhead amortization

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compare eager and compiled latency or throughput over the approved workload; calculate compile overhead versus sustained inference or training gains.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure compiled workloads meet the approved performance target relative to the eager baseline.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch documents torch.compile as a performance feature, so representative validation is necessary.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure exported models match approved reference outputs before deployment

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Validate that torch.export or other deployment-oriented representations preserve model behavior on approved example inputs and benchmark sets.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Export parity pass rate, output difference, exact-match parity

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compare exported-model outputs to the source PyTorch model on approved example inputs and benchmark datasets.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure exported representations match reference outputs within the approved numerical or task-quality tolerance.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorchâ€™s torch.export is intended for Python-less environments, so export parity is a key deployment control.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure exported and deployed model artifacts retain lineage to the source PyTorch model

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Maintain lineage from the source training checkpoint to exported deployment artifacts, including code version, example inputs, and export settings.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Completeness = deployed artifacts with linked source model, code version, export settings, and benchmark evidence / total deployed artifacts.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure complete lineage exists for all deployed PyTorch-derived model artifacts.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch is often the source framework even when final deployment occurs elsewhere, so lineage matters for auditability.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure quantized models preserve approved quality relative to non-quantized baselines

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Re-benchmark quantized models against the approved FP32 or higher-precision reference before deployment or production use.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Accuracy retention, exact-match delta, perplexity delta

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compare quantized-model task metrics to the reference model over the approved benchmark set.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure quantized-model quality retention remains above threshold and task-quality degradation remains within approved limits.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: Quantization support is part of PyTorchâ€™s model optimization landscape, so post-quantization validation is appropriate.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure privacy-focused red-team evaluation is performed for PyTorch-trained models

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Evaluate PyTorch models for PII leakage or memorization risks using seeded prompts, examples, or extraction tests appropriate to the model type.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Leakage rate = successful PII disclosures / total seeded privacy test cases; compute detection precision and recall where privacy classifiers are used.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure PII leakage rate remains below threshold and privacy-detection recall remains above threshold.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch does not provide the evaluation by itself, but PyTorch-trained models should still be governed against privacy leakage risk.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure fairness benchmarks are evaluated for every release candidate

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Run fairness evaluations over demographic or subgroup-sensitive benchmark sets before promoting PyTorch-trained models.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Demographic parity difference, subgroup error rate, CrowS-Pairs or BBQ score

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compute subgroup disparities or benchmark fairness scores across the approved evaluation set.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure subgroup disparity remains below threshold and fairness benchmark scores remain within approved bounds.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch is the training framework, so fairness evaluation is part of model-release governance rather than a framework-enforced feature.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure hallucination and faithfulness are re-evaluated after major PyTorch model changes

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: When model architecture, training data, loss functions, optimization strategy, or precision settings change, rerun faithfulness and hallucination evaluations before release.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Faithfulness = supported claims / total claims; hallucination rate = unsupported answers / total evaluated answers on the benchmark set.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure faithfulness remains above threshold and hallucination rate remains below threshold after major model changes.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: This is particularly relevant for PyTorch-trained generative models and LLMs.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure toxicity benchmarks are measured for PyTorch-trained user-facing models

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Evaluate release candidates for toxic-generation behavior before deployment, especially for conversational or generative use cases.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Score benchmark outputs with a toxicity classifier and compute average toxicity plus the share of outputs exceeding the approved threshold.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure average toxicity and toxic-output rate remain below approved thresholds for release candidates.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch is often the framework used to fine-tune or train these models, so this is a relevant release-gating rule.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure factuality and unsupported-claim metrics are benchmarked for release candidates

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Evaluate PyTorch-trained generative models for unsupported claims and factuality before approving deployment.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Unsupported-claim rate = unsupported claims / total claims; factuality score from the approved evaluator on the benchmark set.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure unsupported-claim rate remains below threshold and factuality remains above threshold.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: Applicable mainly to LLM or generative systems built or fine-tuned in PyTorch.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure training checkpoints are validated and restorable

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Validate that model checkpoints can be loaded and resume training or evaluation correctly before they are accepted as recovery points.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Restore success rate = successfully reloaded and resumed checkpoints / total tested checkpoints.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure checkpoint restore success remains above the approved threshold for all release or recovery checkpoints.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch training commonly depends on checkpointing, so checkpoint integrity is a practical framework-level control.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure representative workloads stay within approved memory budgets

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Measure memory usage under representative training and inference workloads to detect configurations likely to fail in production or scale-out.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Peak memory = maximum observed device or host memory use during the workload; OOM rate = failed runs due to memory exhaustion / total runs.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure representative workloads stay within approved memory budgets and OOM rates remain below threshold.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch workloads are especially sensitive to tensor sizes, batch sizes, and model architecture choices.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure runtime environment compatibility is validated for each release artifact

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Record and validate the PyTorch version, CUDA or accelerator stack, dependency versions, and target hardware assumptions for each approved model artifact.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Pass rate = target environments passing compatibility validation / total required target environments.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure all required deployment environments pass compatibility validation before release.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch behavior can vary by runtime stack and hardware backend, so environment governance is important.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure every released model has complete lineage from code, data, and checkpoint artifacts

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Track source code revision, dataset version, training configuration, random seed policy, checkpoints, and deployment artifact lineage for every release candidate.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Completeness = released models with all required lineage fields and linked artifacts / total released models.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure model-lineage completeness is 100% before release approval.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: This aligns well with model-card expectations and is especially important for PyTorch-trained model governance.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure reproducibility settings and expected nondeterminism are documented for governed workloads

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Record reproducibility settings, random seeds, deterministic flags, and known nondeterministic operators for training and evaluation runs.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Completeness = documented reproducibility fields / total required reproducibility fields; repeated-run variance from identical runs under the same setup.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure reproducibility documentation is complete and repeated-run variance remains within the approved tolerance.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch users commonly need to manage determinism explicitly, so this is a realistic governance and reliability rule.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure DataLoader and input pipeline throughput do not bottleneck training or inference

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Profile and validate DataLoader performance so worker count, shuffling, transforms, and storage access do not create avoidable idle time.

props.name: Associated_Metric
props.value: Input pipeline throughput, idle ratio, data wait time

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Compute items per second delivered by the input pipeline and the fraction of step time spent waiting for data.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure input pipeline throughput meets the approved target and data wait time remains below threshold.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: This is a common PyTorch-specific performance issue because DataLoader configuration can dominate training efficiency.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure release testing covers quality, safety, fairness, privacy, robustness, and deployment parity

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Build a PyTorch release standard that evaluates accuracy, numerical stability, fairness, toxicity, privacy leakage, export parity, and runtime compatibility instead of checking only headline quality metrics.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Coverage = number of mandated PyTorch risk domains with active automated tests / total mandated risk domains in the release standard.

props.name: HF_Metric
props.value: Composite evaluation coverage based on benchmark families

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure automated release-test coverage remains at or above threshold across the required validation domains.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: PyTorch is broad enough that release governance should span model quality, systems behavior, and deployment correctness.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure released PyTorch models have complete model-card-style documentation

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Document intended use, limitations, training data scope, evaluation benchmarks, fairness results, privacy assumptions, and deployment constraints for each released model.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Completeness = completed required transparency fields / total required model transparency fields for each released model.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure model transparency completeness is 100% before production approval.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: This directly aligns PyTorch model governance with Hugging Face model-card expectations.

props.name: Rule_Title
props.value: Ensure training and deployment architecture assumptions are documented

props.name: Rule_Description
props.value: Document hardware assumptions, distributed topology, export path, runtime dependencies, optimizer strategy, and known operational constraints for each governed PyTorch system.

props.name: Metric_Calculation
props.value: Completeness = documented required architecture and dependency fields / total required fields in the approved transparency checklist.

props.name: Metric_Based_Rule
props.value: Ensure system transparency completeness is 100% before production approval.

props.name: Mapping_Notes
props.value: This is especially relevant for PyTorch because the same model may be trained, exported, and deployed through different stacks.

control-implementations.description: Implementation of NIST AI RMF controls for PyTorch
